thesis: Howard Marks argues that while there is ambiguity in defining a bubble in artificial intelligence, he distinguishes between the behavior of companies within the industry and the behavior of investors regarding the industry, choosing to focus primarily on the latter. He suggests that bubbles result from applying excessive optimism to new developments, leading to irrational exuberance where asset prices are not justified by predictable earning power, and notes that history can impose limits on awe regarding the present and imagination regarding the future.
